VERDICT: REJECT

The proposed value t = q^(2h) fails a direct check in the case h = 1, which is a valid instance of the setup.

With h = 1, the (h−1)-spaces are points, so X is a point set in PG(3,q) with at most t points on any plane and |X| = (t−2)q + t. For t = q², this gives |X| = q³ + q² − 2q. The space PG(3,q) has q³ + q² + q + 1 points, so the complement has exactly q + 1 points. Each plane has q² + q + 1 points, so it must meet the complement in at least (q² + q + 1) − t = q + 1 points. That forces all q + 1 complement points into every plane. Since the planes have empty common intersection, this is impossible. So t = q² cannot occur for h = 1.

The proposed generalization t = q^((k−2)h) is therefore unsupported. The k = 3 claim (t = q^h) is also doubtful as a general pattern, since for h = 1 the known maximal-arc theory gives a divisibility condition rather than a single value. For k = 4 and h = 1, the natural candidate is t = q, which would suggest t = q^h, but I have not verified the literature result, so I cannot give the correct value with certainty.

CONFIDENCE: 4
